summary: Six-lens Board3 pre-fab review (inline reviewer instructions) with adversarial verification of high-severity findings
logs: 6 CRITICAL/HIGH findings queued for adversarial verification, 22 MEDIUM/LOW passed through unverified

reviewerVerdicts.verdict: DRC-CLEAN. Board3 (kicad/board3/ProPrj_New Project_2026-07-15_23-14-34_2026-07-27.kicad_pcb, current HEAD of fix/board3-warning-inbox) reports 0 DRC violations and 0 unconnected items, confirmed independently two ways: (1) mcp__kicad__run_drc against the live, correctly-configured project -> "Found 0 DRC violations" (0 error/0 warning/0 info); (2) tools/kicad_verify.py, which stages the board with the project's real (non-stock-default) rules from kicad_rules.json and runs kicad-cli headless -> 0 violations, 0 unconnected, advisory "drills below the 0.3mm cost floor: 0.2mm" carried over unchanged (pre-existing, non-blocking, documented). Baseline (main @ merge-base 8158151, i.e. the board before this branch's only copper-touching commit 25193d2) independently re-measured the same way: 35 real DRC errors (courtyards_overlap x25, copper_edge_clearance x10) + 115 real warnings (track_dangling x12, via_dangling x1, silk_edge_clearance x3, hole_to_hole x11, silk_overlap x53, silk_over_copper x35) = 150 real violations, all resolved to 0 on the current tip. NEW = 0 by kicad_verify's identity-based diff (catches type-swaps, not just count parity), so no violation was traded for another. A --severity-all lib_footprint_issues count of 120 appears identically in both baseline and current boards -- confirmed to be a tool-staging artifact (kicad-cli run against a board copy lacking its footprint .pretty library directories), not a real board defect; the branch's own commit message independently names this same class of noise. Net connectivity: independently re-derived via a standalone pcbnew script (not the MCP, not regex) -- every net with >2 pads on the current board (including /GND 134 pads, /+3V3 75, /+5V 50 -- the historically risky telltale daisy-chain net -- plus 27 other 3-pad nets) has every one of its pads mutually reachable in the connectivity graph; no orphaned pads, no broken daisy chains. Copper zones independently enumerated via pcbnew: 3 filled /GND zones (Top/Bottom/Inner1), 1 filled /+5V zone (Inner2), plus rule-area keepouts that are netless by definition -- matches expected zone topology, nothing netless that should carry a net. This branch's diff touches exactly one commit that modifies the .kicad_pcb (25193d2, "zero the DRC warning inbox"), and it is delete-only/respace-only per its own description (dangling-copper removal under a per-item connectivity guard that reverts on any airwire increase, via respacing, one thermal-relief fix, silk cleanup, footprint-library normalization) -- no net reassignment, no footprint replacement, so the daisy-chain-topology risk this review specifically screens for does not apply here. The other two board-adjacent commits on the branch (a995349: adds missing JLCImport library/3D-model files only, no .kicad_pcb change; 4b717b8: one-line fix to tools/kicad_freeroute.py itself) do not touch board copper, so the freerouting-specific checks (1.9.0 vs 2.2.4, locked-copper survival) do not apply -- no autorouting event is in this diff.

Per-subsystem verdicts (not averaged):

- POR/Strapping: FAILS. The one specific, quantified vendor requirement checked (AW9523B RSTN sequencing) is violated on both instances.
- Protection (overcurrent): FAILS. No fuse/PTC exists anywhere in the BOM on either external power input.
- Protection (reverse-polarity / ESD): HOLDS, verified. Ideal-diode ORing (U5/U6+Q1/Q2) covers reverse-polarity on both DC-barrel and USB inputs; USBLC6-2SC6 covers USB ESD; TJA1051's datasheet-rated ±8kV IEC61000-4-2 covers the bare CAN screw terminals without needing an external TVS.
- Power (rail sizing/margin): HOLDS BUT UNVERIFIED. USB-C/CH224K + barrel ORing topology is sound; the +3V3 bulk (440uF on C2/C16) sits ~6.5x above the TPS563201's own documented D-CAP2-stable Cout window (20-68uF) -- a real, already-partially-analyzed-by-the-team but still-live risk on the current board, not something this session newly found but confirmed still present. Backlight/LED worst-case current budget cannot be closed because the project's own docs record the Riverdi backlight current as unknown (gated, not this review's gap).
- Decoupling: HOLDS BUT THIN. AW9523B VCC bypass caps (C61/C62, 100nF) sit at the low end of the part's own published CIN window (0.1/1/100 uF) and 10x under the value shown in both of the datasheet's own typical application circuits (1uF), placed ~4.5-5.5mm center-to-center from the IC, not verified against the actual LED-driver switching load.
- Signal integrity (SPI to panels): HOLDS BUT UNVERIFIED, and the bench numbers in CLAUDE.md do not apply here. Board3 uses three fully independent SPI peripherals (SPI1/PA5-7 center, SPI2/PB13-15 left, SPI4/PE2+PE5+PE6 right), each isolated by its own 33-ohm series resistor -- a materially different, better topology than the Teensy/F767 bench rigs' shared-bus wiring, and it structurally avoids the documented two-panel shared-bus crosstalk mechanism by construction. But no clock rate for this specific H755 hardware has ever been bench-soaked; the 8/13.5 MHz figures in CLAUDE.md belong to unrelated bring-up boards.
- Signal integrity (I2C bus): HOLDS BUT UNVERIFIED. R5/R8 = 4.7kOhm to +3.3V was flagged by the project's own plan as "check at execution, drop toward 2.2-4.7k if edges sag" -- that check has not happened; a rough capacitance estimate puts the 10-90% rise time close to or over Fast-mode's 300ns budget.
- Documentation/schematic hygiene: FAILS as a process matter (not an electrical defect). Multiple free-floating schematic text annotations describe an architecture the board no longer has (a ULN2803A-class driver "U10" plus eight discrete series resistors R25-R48 that do not exist in the current BOM, and "Waveshare SN65HVD230 CAN breakout modules" where the board actually has on-board TJA1051 transceivers) and were never removed across the I2C-revision rewrite.

Overall: the board is not fab-ready from an electrical-robustness standpoint independent of its already-tracked DRC/routing work. The POR/strapping and overcurrent-protection findings are new, concrete, and datasheet/BOM-sourced; they should be closed before fabrication. Full EasyEDA-side verification (ERC/power-tree/simulate tools) could not be performed this session because the bridge was never connected -- treat this as a KiCad-copy-only review, not a full authoritative-source review.

Board3 has already been through a rigorous "does this earn its place" pass on itself: dual CAN, ideal-diode power-OR, and buttons-on-GPIO-vs-expander were all explicitly evaluated with recorded rationale (KTD5, layout-guide current budget, KTD20), and the one clear over-provisioning case found in the project's own history (880uF of clustered THT bulk caps) was already cut to 66uF sited at the loads. One real, modest opportunity remains: the USB-PD trigger IC (U4, CH224K) is a 100W/20V-capable negotiator wired into a board that only ever uses 5V, with no documented reason for the extra range -- worth a one-line confirmation with Kevin, not a mandatory fix. Nothing found qualifies as load-bearing protection removed under cover of simplification.

Board3, as it stands today on fix/board3-warning-inbox (250.254 x 50.254 mm, 4-layer, 144 footprints), passes a live re-run of KiCad's own DRC at BOTH error and warning severity with zero findings, using a project file whose staged design rules (0.1016 mm clearance, 0.1016 mm min track, 0.15 mm min annular ring, 0.2 mm min through-hole) match JLCPCB's live-confirmed published capability numbers for a 4-layer standard 1oz board. That is a genuinely clean result, independently re-verified this session (not taken from the plan docs, which describe an intermediate state). No finding below rises to EXCEEDS CAPABILITY -- I found no case where measured geometry breaches a JLCPCB limit I could confirm live. The real risk on this board is concentrated in exactly the class of thing DRC cannot see: no per-layer stackup is recorded anywhere in the KiCad project (only the aggregate 1.6 mm board thickness), so every copper-weight and dielectric assumption used for the USB/CAN impedance math is an inference, never confirmed against an actual order or JLCPCB's calculator; the differential pairs are not routed to a verified target gap (measured USB and CAN2 both sit near a 0.15 mm edge gap, appropriate for USB's 90 ohm but the opposite of what CAN's 120 ohm wants, while CAN1's legs run uncoupled for most of their length); and the board's via population sits at, not above, JLCPCB's absolute-minimum annular ring with one known via-in-pad on a live MCU signal pin. None of these fail a JLCPCB capability ceiling I can point to -- they are unconfirmed design margins on a board otherwise ready to order.

confirmedFindings.summary: AW9523B RSTN pin (U11 pin 23, U12 pin 23) is wired directly onto the /+5V rail with no series R/RC delay, violating the datasheet's mandatory ~100us RSTN-low-hold-after-VCC power-on sequencing requirement on both telltale-driver ICs.
confirmedFindings.evidence: Netlist proof (kicad-cli sch export netlist against kicad/board3/ProPrj_New Project_2026-07-15_23-14-34_2026-07-27.kicad_sch): net code 2, name "/+5V", contains both 'U11 pin=23 RSTN_23' and 'U12 pin=23 RSTN_23' as members of the SAME net as VCC -- i.e. zero series impedance, not a separate '/RSTN' net joined by a resistor. AWINIC AW9523B datasheet (Mar 2024 V2.4), POWER ON section: 'After power-up, about 100us delay is required before RSTN set to high, otherwise, the device may work incorrectly. The minimal wait time for I2C communication is 5ms' (Figure 6, AW9523B Power On, shows RSTN as a distinct signal held low for ~100us after VBAT establishes, not tied to VBAT). Also confirmed: R_RSTN internal pull-low = 100kOhm typ (datasheet DC table), meaning the chip's own default is low and someone chose to override it with a hard tie to +5V rather than an RC delay. This is the ONLY passive safety mechanism protecting the eight telltale LEDs now that the series resistors and the DMOS driver were deliberately removed (KTD17) in favor of relying on the AD-pin-strapped POR-default GPIO-output-HIGH state (verified separately: both ICs strap AD1=+5V, landing on Table 1's row that drives P1_4-P1_7 HIGH = zero LED differential at POR) -- but that entire safety argument depends on the chip's internal POR/reset logic completing correctly, which the vendor explicitly says requires this sequencing step that the board does not implement.
confirmedFindings.recommendation: Add an RC delay (or a dedicated reset supervisor/PMIC reset output) between /+5V and RSTN on both U11 and U12 so RSTN is held low for >=100us after VCC establishes, per Figure 6. If the board must keep RSTN hard-tied to VCC, this needs a bench soak across many power cycles (including fast brownout/recovery, which a vehicle 12V/5V rail will produce) to prove the POR-default GPIO state is reliably reached before firmware ever gets to write LED-mode registers -- not just asserted from the datasheet's default-state table.

confirmedFindings.summary: No fuse or PTC/polyfuse exists anywhere on Board3's BOM, so neither external power input (DC barrel jack DC1, nor USB-C via CH224K) has any overcurrent/short-circuit protection on this board -- only reverse-polarity ORing.
confirmedFindings.evidence: Full BOM (fab_audit/bom.csv, 51 lines) contains L1 (ferrite bead, not a fuse) and L2 (buck inductor) but no fuse/PPTC/resettable-fuse part class anywhere. Netlist confirms DC1 (barrel jack) feeds directly into Q2 (AO4406A MOSFET) gated by U6 (LM74700 ideal-diode controller) for reverse-polarity/ORing onto /+5V_BARREL -- there is no current-sense or current-limit element in that path. A stale schematic annotation (kicad/board3/...kicad_sch line 14897: '(text "J1: +5V IN (dedicated 5V/15A supply)"') suggests the intended supply is rated well beyond what any downstream trace/connector/component on this board could be expected to survive under a fault, with nothing upstream of the board to limit it.
confirmedFindings.recommendation: Add a resettable PTC fuse (or a fuse plus the existing ideal-diode path) sized to the actual expected load on the +5V_BARREL input, sited between DC1 and Q2/U6. Re-verify or remove the stale '5V/15A' annotation once the real supply spec is confirmed -- if 15A is real, the gap is more severe, not less.

confirmedFindings.summary: The AW9523BTQR footprint (used by both U11 and U12) has zero F.CrtYd/B.CrtYd geometry anywhere in its definition — confirmed by reading both full footprint blocks in the .kicad_pcb (lines ~17043 and ~45283) end-to-end and by a whole-file grep for F.CrtYd/B.CrtYd matching 0 occurrences inside either block.

Manually reconstructing U12's package envelope (safe to do without full rotation math since a 4x4mm QFN is square and rotation-invariant in bbox) puts its body edge within ~0.4-0.55mm of neighboring LED6's real body (LED6 body_bbox from the one successful tool call: 223.5-226 x 93.55-97.45; U12 body ≈225-229 x 98-102) — tight, and never checked by any tool this session. Placement-only (no routing implication observed).

Manually eyeball U12 vs. LED6 in the KiCad 2D view in the meantime.

confirmedFindings.subsystem: Polarity marking — telltale LEDs LED4, LED6, LED7
confirmedFindings.summary: Three of the eight telltale LEDs (LED4 = HL-A-3528H203BC-S1-13HL; LED6 and LED7 = HL-A-3528S35FC-S1-13HL) have no cathode/pin-1 indicator on the physical F.SilkS silkscreen — only two plain symmetric parallel lines forming a rectangle outline. A polarity triangle exists in the same footprint but only on F.Fab (Component Marking Layer), which is not printed silkscreen ink.
confirmedFindings.evidence: Verified two ways: (1) direct read of both board instances (LED4 at file offset ~17914, LED6 at ~6542) shows exactly 2 fp_line elements on F.SilkS, both plain and symmetric, no asymmetric mark; (2) grep of the master JLCImport.pretty/*.kicad_mod library files for `layer "F.SilkS"` count: HL-A-3528H203BC-S1-13HL.kicad_mod = 3, HL-A-3528S35FC-S1-13HL.kicad_mod = 3 (2 lines + 1 hidden reference-text tag = 0 visible marks), vs. HL-A-3528U51GC-S1-13HL.kicad_mod (LED1/LED2) = 19, HVO-3528CPXA.kicad_mod (LED5) = 17, HL-A-3528S31YC-S1-13HL.kicad_mod (LED8) = 6, HL-A-3528H343W-...kicad_mod (LED3) = 7 — all of which do carry a distinguishing silk mark. Failure mode: a reversed LED4, LED6, or LED7 populates dark or on-the-wrong-telltale with no way to visually confirm correct orientation from the assembled board's silkscreen; this is exactly the 'wrong indicator lit, hard to trace to a placement error' scenario the task brief warns about, and it affects 3 of 8 positions, not a hypothetical.
confirmedFindings.recommendation: Add a visible cathode/pin-1 mark on F.SilkS (not just F.Fab) to the HL-A-3528H203BC-S1-13HL and HL-A-3528S35FC-S1-13HL footprints in JLCImport.pretty before fab, matching the pattern already present in the other four LED footprints on this board.

confirmedFindings.subsystem: Paste stencil — exposed-pad fine-pitch parts (U11, U12, U2)
confirmedFindings.summary: All three exposed-pad SMD parts on the board (U11/U12 AW9523BTQR QFN-24, EP pad '25' = 2.8x2.8mm; U2 W25Q512JVEIQ WSON-8, EP pad '9' = 5.2x4.65mm) use a single solid, unwindowed paste aperture matching 100% of the exposed-pad copper. A whole-board grep for solder_paste_margin / solder_paste_margin_ratio returns 0 matches across all 143 footprints, confirming no paste reduction or windowing exists anywhere, including under these EPs.
confirmedFindings.evidence: Direct pad-definition read: U12 pad 25 `(size 2.8 2.8)` on F.Cu/F.Mask/F.Paste with no segmentation (offset ~45611); U2 pad 9 `(size 5.2 4.65)` identically unwindowed (offset ~17843-434 relative). A large solid paste deposit under a small package traps flux/outgassing during reflow, a well-documented cause of voiding, part float, and tombstoning under exposed pads — standard guidance (JLCPCB SMT notes, IPC-7093) is a checkerboard/grid EP paste pattern at 50-80% coverage. Placement-only (stencil/paste-print risk), no routing consequence.
confirmedFindings.recommendation: Add a windowed (segmented, ~50-70% coverage) paste-aperture pattern to the exposed-pad definitions in the AW9523BTQR and WSON-8 footprints before ordering the stencil.

Live mcp__pcbparts__jlc_get_part(C19702) confirms: model CL10A106KP8NNNC, specs Capacitance=10uF, Voltage Rating=10V, package 0603. The sibling group (C29,C30,C31,C48,C49,C66,C68) correctly uses Supplier Part C45783 (CL21A226MAQNNNE, live-confirmed 22uF/25V/0805) with the same Value="22uF" label -- C67 looks like a copy/paste leftover that kept the group's old Value text after being re-pointed to the 10uF part. Two `kicad_interface.py` processes were observed running concurrently on this machine (PIDs 8264 and 33472) -- worth confirming with Kevin whether one is stale/orphaned before anyone restarts either, since they may be shared across concurrent agent sessions the way the EasyEDA bridge is.

passthroughFindings.summary: The +3V3 rail's bulk capacitance (C2 + C16 = 440uF electrolytic) is roughly 6.5x above the TPS563201's own documented D-CAP2 loop-stability window (20-68uF, SLVSD90B Table 7-2 / SLVAF11), a real and currently-unresolved risk on the board as it stands today.
passthroughFindings.evidence: This is carried forward from the project's own plan (docs/plans/2026-07-27-003-...-plan.md, Open Questions/U13-U14), which did the datasheet legwork (SLVSD90B Table 7-2, SLVAF11 Sec 3.1, SLVA905 Table 4) and concluded more bulk capacitance lowers crossover frequency and degrades phase margin for this D-CAP2 topology -- i.e. 'more capacitance is safer' is false here. It remains gated (U13/U14) on an unrelated blocker (Riverdi backlight current), so it is still physically on the board today, unresolved, not a new finding but confirmed still live at this review's snapshot.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Do not treat the backlight-current gate as blocking this specific fix -- the C2/C16 oversizing is independently justified by the buck's own stability spec regardless of backlight current. Reduce toward the 20-68uF window or add local ESR/placement changes per the plan's own U14 approach.

passthroughFindings.summary: AW9523B VCC decoupling (C61 for U11, C62 for U12) is a single 100nF cap centered ~4.5-5.5mm from the IC -- at the minimum of the part's published CIN range and 10x under the value shown in both of the datasheet's own typical application circuits (1uF).
passthroughFindings.evidence: Netlist confirms C61 pin1/C62 pin1 on /+5V and pin2/pin2 on /GND (i.e. genuine VCC-GND bypass caps, not incidentally-nearby parts for something else). BOM confirms both are 100nF (0.1uF), C0603. Board coordinates (parsed from kicad/board3/...kicad_pcb): U11 footprint at (85,95), C61 at (85,89.5) = 5.5mm center-to-center; U12 at (227,100), C62 at (222.5,100) = 4.5mm center-to-center. AWINIC AW9523B datasheet Figures 2 and 4 (typical application circuits) both show a '1uF' capacitor at VCC, and the datasheet's own DC table lists 'CIN Input capacitance 0.1 1 100 uF' (Min/Typ/Max) -- so 100nF is the documented floor, not the documented target, for a part actively current-sourcing up to 4 LED channels at up to ~37mA typ each (IMAX spec) per IC.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Either move to the datasheet's typical 1uF at VCC, or if 100nF is kept, verify on the bench under worst-case all-four-channels-on transient switching that supply droop at the IC does not disturb I2C communication or other loads sharing /+5V at that moment.

passthroughFindings.summary: I2C pull-up sizing (R5/R8 = 4.7kOhm to /+3V3) has not been verified against actual bus capacitance; a rough estimate puts Fast-mode (400kHz) rise time close to or over the 300ns spec limit, and the project's own plan already flagged this as unresolved.
passthroughFindings.evidence: Netlist confirms R5 pin1 on /I2C_SDA, R8 pin1 on /I2C_SCL, both pin2 on /+3V3 (not /+5V) -- 4.7kOhm to 3.3V. docs/plans/2026-07-28-001-...-plan.md states outright: 'R5/R8 pull-up values checked at execution: drop toward 2.2-4.7kOhm if edges sag' -- i.e. this was left as an open, to-be-measured item, not a closed one. Using CI=3pF/pin (datasheet) x2 devices x2 pins, plus FRAM and MCU pin capacitance and an estimated ~200mm trunk (per the same plan's own routing estimate), total bus capacitance plausibly lands in the 60-90pF range; tr ~= 0.8473*R*C at R=4.7k, C=90pF gives ~358ns, over the I2C Fast-mode 300ns budget (NXP UM10204) if the bus is actually run at 400kHz.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Measure actual bus capacitance and rise time on the bench (or via kicad_measure trace-length data) before the board is called fab-ready on this point, and confirm the firmware's actual configured SCL frequency (400kHz per the AW9523B's spec sheet vs a more conservative 100kHz) -- the finding only bites at Fast-mode.

passthroughFindings.summary: Board3's three-panel SPI topology (independent SPI1/SPI2/SPI4 peripherals with per-line 33-ohm series resistors) has never had its own bench soak at any clock rate -- the clock numbers documented in CLAUDE.md belong to unrelated bring-up hardware (Teensy 4.1, NUCLEO-F767ZI), not this board.
passthroughFindings.evidence: Netlist confirms fully independent buses: center panel SCLK/MISO/MOSI on U1 pins PA5/PA6/PA7 (SPI1), left panel on PB13/PB14/PB15 (SPI2), right panel on PE2/PE5(approx)/PE6 (SPI4) -- each MCU-side node routed through its own 33-ohm series resistor (R32-R37 group, confirmed 33-ohm 0603 in BOM) before reaching its FPC connector. This is a materially different (and likely better, since it removes the shared-bus crosstalk mechanism entirely) topology than the bench rigs' single shared SCLK/MISO/MOSI bus with per-panel CS only -- but per the project's own standing rule ('this board's SPI is bench-verified at specific clocks that came from failure at higher clocks, not derivation -- any new speed/tap/topology is unverified until it has its own bench soak'), none of the existing bench data transfers to this hardware.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Before fab (or at minimum before claiming this resolves the two-panel-crosstalk open item), run Board3's actual assembled hardware through the same clock-walk methodology used on the Teensy/F767 rigs, starting conservative and stepping up, rather than assuming the topology change alone is sufficient.

passthroughFindings.summary: Multiple free-floating schematic text annotations describe a completely superseded architecture and were never removed across the I2C-revision rewrite, risking misdirected future assembly or debugging work.
passthroughFindings.evidence: kicad/board3/...kicad_sch, lines 14919 and 14952: describes 'U10' as a Darlington/DMOS telltale driver with eight discrete series resistors R25/R26/R27/R38/R39/R40/R44/R48 wired 'off-board' -- none of these resistors or U10 exist in the current BOM (fab_audit/bom.csv has no U10 and no R25-R48 as individual telltale resistors; the design moved to AW9523B constant-current LED-mode drive with zero series resistors per KTD17). Lines 14963 and 14974: describes 'CN4/CN5: Waveshare SN65HVD230 CAN breakout modules' -- the board actually has on-board TJA1051 transceivers (U8/U9), not external breakout modules; this text was never updated when the on-board transceivers landed.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Delete or rewrite these annotations to match the as-built AW9523B/TJA1051 architecture (or explicitly mark them 'HISTORICAL/SUPERSEDED') so a future reader building or debugging from the schematic does not act on wiring instructions for hardware that no longer exists.

passthroughFindings.summary: This review could not reach the EasyEDA authoritative source at all -- the bridge was not connected and the EasyEDA Pro desktop app was not even running -- so every finding above is against the KiCad copy only, and conversion is documented as one-way.
passthroughFindings.evidence: easyeda_bridge_status and easyeda_health_check both returned bridge_connected:false; PowerShell process listing found no EasyEDA process running on the workstation at all. kicad/README.md states the KiCad copy does not round-trip with EasyEDA.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Re-run this review (or at least the ERC/power-tree/simulate steps: easyeda_semantic_erc_validate, easyeda_power_tree_analyze, easyeda_simulate_operating_point) once EasyEDA Pro is open and the bridge extension toggled, since that is the actual source of truth per this project's own stated rules.

passthroughFindings.summary: U4 is a 100W/5-20V USB-PD 3.0 trigger controller, but Board3's power tree only ever consumes 5V, and the chip's legacy fast-charge protocols (QC/AFC/FCP) are wired inert.
passthroughFindings.evidence: Pad-net dump of U3 (TPS563201) shows VIN tied directly to /+5V -- no 9/12/20V net exists anywhere on the board (full schematic label sweep: +5V, +5V_BARREL, +3V3, VBUS, GND only). U4's CFG2/CFG3 pads read unconnected-(U4-CFG2/3-PadX) and CFG1 ties straight to /CH224_VDD (a fixed low-voltage strap). U4's DP/DM pads (4/5) are also unconnected-(U4-DP/DM-PadX), so the D+/D- based QC2.0/3.0/AFC/FCP paths the chip supports are never used -- only its PD-3.0 CC1/CC2 path (pins 6/7) is live. No plan or KTD (checked docs/plans/2026-07-24-001-feat-board3-h755-carrier-plan.md R18, the only power-entry requirement) calls for negotiated voltages above 5V; the part appears with zero documented rationale on an otherwise heavily KTD-annotated board. jlc_find_alternatives(C970725) surfaces the same vendor's CH221K (C5125736, SOT-23-6, $0.33 vs $0.49 @qty1, 6 pins vs 10) offering the same PD-3.0 sink function actually used.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Confirm with Kevin whether higher-voltage PD negotiation is wanted for a future revision. If not, downgrade U4 to a 5V-only/lower-power PD sink part (e.g. CH221K) to cut BOM cost and pin count. Blast radius: schematic value/metadata edit is trivial, but CH221K's package differs (SOT-23-6 vs ESSOP-10), so per the project's own KTD12 rule this requires Kevin's GUI 'Update PCB from Schematic' step and re-placement, not a pure property edit -- not a same-footprint swap like U10's driver change.

passthroughFindings.summary: No per-layer stackup block exists in the KiCad project -- only the aggregate board thickness (1.6 mm) is recorded -- so copper weight, prepreg/core dielectric, and layer order are nowhere encoded as an actual order spec.
passthroughFindings.evidence: kicad/board3/ProPrj_New Project_2026-07-15_23-14-34_2026-07-27.kicad_pcb line 6: `(general (thickness 1.6))`, no `(stackup ...)` node anywhere in the file (grep for `stackup` returns nothing). tools/kicad_rules.json's own `$stackup_assumption` field says explicitly: 'The importer carried NO stackup block, so impedance is computed against JLCPCB's standard 4-layer 1.6 mm stackup (JLC04161H-7628) ... CONFIRM against JLCPCB's own impedance calculator before fabrication.' I independently confirmed via live web search that JLC04161H-7628 (35 um/1oz outer copper, 0.2104 mm 7628 prepreg, 1.065 mm core) is in fact JLCPCB's real default 4-layer 1.6 mm template, so the assumption is currently correct -- but nothing in the repo enforces that the actual order matches it, and no fab-order artifact (kicad/board3/jlcpcb/project.db's `metadata` table is empty; no stackup file exists) records copper weight as a locked parameter.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Before submitting to JLCPCB, explicitly select/confirm the 4-layer 1.6 mm 1oz stackup in the order form and, ideally, write a `(stackup)` block into the .kicad_pcb (or a checked-in fab spec) so a future re-order or a different board size can't silently drift onto a different template.

passthroughFindings.subsystem: Controlled impedance (USB HS pair, CAN1/CAN2 pairs)
passthroughFindings.summary: USB and CAN differential pairs are not routed to a verified or even consistent target gap; direct measurement of the routed copper shows CAN2's tightest approach matches USB's tight-coupling gap rather than CAN's required loose gap, and CAN1's legs are not coupled for most of their run.
passthroughFindings.evidence: No impedance netclass exists in KiCad (get_design_rules / the .kicad_pro carry no per-pair impedance target). I measured actual routed-segment proximity directly from the .kicad_pcb: USB_DP/USB_DM closest approach ~0.406 mm center-to-center (~0.15 mm edge gap, matching kicad_rules.json's own USB target note); CAN2_H/CAN2_L closest approach ~0.406 mm center-to-center (~0.15 mm edge gap) -- but kicad_rules.json states CAN needs a >=0.5 mm gap to approach its 120 ohm target, and a 0.15 mm gap pulls Zdiff toward USB's ~90 ohm range instead; CAN1_H/CAN1_L closest approach is ~1.08 mm center-to-center, and tools/kicad_netclass.json itself documents 'Neither CAN pair is tightly coupled between transceiver and terminal block.' kicad_rules.json's own differential-pairs section is written entirely as target values with 'CONFIRM against JLCPCB's own impedance calculator' -- i.e. the repo's own record is that this was never done.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Before fab, decide whether CAN's 120 ohm target is actually load-bearing at 1 Mbps (the repo's own analysis argues it mostly isn't, given symmetry/skew already fixed in U6) -- if it is wanted, CAN2's gap needs opening to >=0.5 mm; if not, retire the 120 ohm target from kicad_rules.json rather than leaving it as an unmet, unverified spec next to a design that does something else.

passthroughFindings.summary: The via population is not merely capable of hitting JLCPCB's minimum annular ring -- the great majority of vias on the board (including the default via used almost everywhere) sit exactly at that floor, with zero margin.
passthroughFindings.evidence: Direct extraction of all via size/drill pairs from the .kicad_pcb: 98 vias at 0.6/0.3 mm (ring 0.150 mm), 100 vias at 0.61/0.305 mm (ring 0.1525 mm, the U7 thermal-via batch), and 1 via at 0.5/0.2 mm (ring 0.15 mm, the documented U1.93 via-in-pad). Live-fetched JLCPCB capability: annular ring 'recommended 0.20mm or above; absolute minimum 0.15mm' for 1oz multilayer. So ~198 of ~199 vias on this board are within 0.0025 mm of JLC's hard floor, not merely inside it.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Bump the board-wide default via to something with real margin (e.g. 0.7/0.35 mm, giving a 0.175 mm ring, or to JLC's recommended 0.20 mm ring outright) before ordering -- registration tolerance at the fab means a via at the absolute floor is a realistic breakout/yield risk even though it nominally passes DRC.

passthroughFindings.summary: One via still sits inside a live SMD signal pad on the MCU (U1 pin 93 / BTN1 net), a documented, unresolved reflow risk that KiCad's DRC cannot see at all.
passthroughFindings.evidence: tools/kicad_rules.json and docs/plans/2026-07-27-002-fix-board3-fab-ready-in-kicad-plan.md both record this as a deliberate residual: '0.10 mm against JLC's published 0.15 mm absolute minimum ... 0.5/0.2 gives exactly 0.15 mm ... Residual, recorded not fixed: it is still a via in a pad.' I confirmed it is still present: exactly one 0.2 mm-drilled via exists on the current board (grep for `(drill 0.2)` returns a single hit), matching the recorded U1.93 exception. Via-in-pad is not a KiCad DRC rule (confirmed: the live full-severity DRC run I performed reports 0 violations of any kind, so this would never surface from that gate alone).
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Resolve before fab if possible (JLCPCB's plugged/tented via-in-pad option, or a re-plan of the BTN1-4/+3V3 escape fan per the plan's own notes) -- an unplugged via barrel in a small pad can wick solder off the joint during reflow on a functioning MCU I/O pin.

passthroughFindings.summary: The project's own DRC configuration sets minimum silk-to-pad clearance to 0.0 mm, meaning a silkscreen element fully overlapping a pad would never be flagged; I could not exhaustively verify the absence of such overlaps across all 144 footprints in the time available.
passthroughFindings.evidence: kicad/board3/ProPrj_New Project_2026-07-15_23-14-34_2026-07-27.kicad_pro: `board.design_settings.rules.min_silk_clearance = 0.0`. A live, full-severity kicad-cli DRC run against the real board (not a staged copy) returned 0 violations of any type/severity, but with that threshold this specific check is structurally blind, matching the task brief's own warning that KiCad's generic DRC usually doesn't check this. Git diff main...HEAD shows several library footprints (C0603, C0805, CRYSTAL-SMD, LQFP-144, USB-C, SW-TH, R0603) had their silkscreen reference-designator positions changed on this branch, but those are in the disconnected ProPrj_New-easyedapro.pretty library, not the board's own embedded footprint copies (U0 in the fab-ready plan explicitly left 'update board footprints to link to exported footprints' unticked), so the board's actual silkscreen was not touched by that diff.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Set min_silk_clearance to a real value (JLC's own live-confirmed minimum pad-to-silk clearance is 0.15 mm) and re-run DRC, or do a visual pass in the KiCad 3D/2D viewer over the fine-pitch parts (U1, U11, U12) before ordering, since this check currently cannot fail even if a real overlap exists.

passthroughFindings.subsystem: Drill size range and aspect ratio
passthroughFindings.summary: All drill sizes on the board (0.2-3.2 mm) sit within JLCPCB's published 0.15-6.3 mm range, but I could not confirm a specific maximum aspect-ratio limit for their standard (non-advanced) 4-layer process from a live source, so the 8:1 ratio implied by the 0.2 mm via-in-pad against the 1.6 mm board thickness is unverified rather than confirmed-passing.
passthroughFindings.evidence: Extracted from the board file: drill sizes present are 0.2 mm (x1), 0.3/0.305 mm (x198, vias), 1.0/1.1/1.2/1.3 mm (x37, header/switch pads), 3.2 mm (x4, likely mounting holes). Live web fetch of jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities confirmed the 0.15-6.3 mm drill range and the annular-ring numbers, but did not surface an explicit aspect-ratio ceiling for the standard process in the content retrieved.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: If a definitive aspect-ratio figure matters for the 0.2 mm via-in-pad decision, get it from JLCPCB support or an account-specific quote rather than assuming; do not treat this note as either a pass or a fail.

passthroughFindings.summary: P1 and P2 (WJ500V-5.08-2P terminal blocks) sit only ~0.195mm from the board's bottom edge (courtyard-to-Edge.Cuts clearance), and DC1 (DC-005-2 barrel jack) sits only ~0.224mm from the left/bottom edge — both well inside typical PCB routing/depaneling tolerance (±0.1-0.2mm).
passthroughFindings.evidence: Computed from validated courtyard-rectangle transform (position + rotation applied to each footprint's F.CrtYd geometry, cross-checked against the one tool-verified courtyard I obtained for LED6 before the backend hung, which matched to within 0.05mm). Board outline confirmed via direct Edge.Cuts vertex read: straight edges at x=25/275 (y 90-130) and y=85/135 (x 30-270). Placement-only; a 0.1-0.2mm edge-routing deviation could clip the connector's mounting flange/shell.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Nudge P1, P2, and DC1 inward by at least 0.3-0.5mm from the board edge, or confirm with the fab house that their edge-routing tolerance is tighter than ±0.1mm for this run.

passthroughFindings.summary: USBC1 (USB-C receptacle) courtyard extends ~0.37mm past the board's left edge (courtyard x-range 24.63-33.37mm vs. board left edge at x=25mm, straight run y=90-130mm).
passthroughFindings.evidence: Computed from the same validated courtyard transform; the connector's real solder pads (through-hole shield legs) stay a safe >3mm from the edge, so this is not a solder-defect risk, but the courtyard-boundary violation is exactly what check_courtyard_overlaps' include_boundary option is designed to catch, and it does mean the part was placed with zero courtyard margin against the panel edge.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Low urgency given real pads are clear, but worth a 0.5mm inward nudge or an explicit board-outline exception if the overhang is intentional (edge-launch connector design).

passthroughFindings.subsystem: Courtyard overlap — U3 (TPS563201 buck regulator) vs L2 (2.2uH inductor)
passthroughFindings.summary: U3 and L2 courtyards overlap by 0.254 x 4.3mm along their facing edge.
passthroughFindings.evidence: From full-board courtyard-vs-courtyard overlap scan (137 of 139 footprints have courtyard geometry; this was the largest non-U1-related overlap). A follow-up pads_bbox check for this pair showed no pad-to-pad overlap, so this reads as tight-but-typical close-coupled buck-converter layout rather than a body collision — but the 4.3mm-long encroachment along one edge is large enough to warrant a manual look, since U3 (SOT-23-6, ~1.4mm) and L2 (shielded power inductor, likely ~2-3mm) also have a height mismatch that could affect paste-print consistency if they end up any closer.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Nudge L2 or U3 by ~0.3mm to clear courtyard margins cleanly, or confirm in the GUI that the actual bodies have adequate clearance.

passthroughFindings.subsystem: Courtyard overlap — U1 (STM32H755 LQFP-144) vs 18 nearby decoupling caps/crystal/resistors
passthroughFindings.summary: U1's footprint courtyard is drawn at ±12.05mm (24.1mm square) around a 20mm-body/22mm-lead-span LQFP-144, which — once the true 22mm lead span is accounted for — is only ~1.05mm beyond the outermost lead tips (a normal margin, not oversized as first appeared). This still causes courtyard-level overlap with 18 closely-placed decoupling caps (0.065-1.4mm), which is typical/expected for tight MCU decoupling. One of these (C40) additionally shows a pad-envelope overlap (~0.55 x 1.4mm) with U1's outer lead row.
passthroughFindings.evidence: Courtyard rect read directly from file (fp_rect ±12.05mm at file offset ~7195) and cross-checked against the footprint's own '...LS22.0...' (22mm lead-span) name. The 17 other overlap pairs showed no pad-bbox overlap in a follow-up check, consistent with normal close-decoupling practice, not a defect. C40 is the one exception worth a manual look since its pad envelope reaches inside U1's own lead-tip line by ~0.5mm.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Spot-check C40's placement against U1's outer pin row in the KiCad 2D editor; the other 17 caps are very likely fine as normal tight decoupling and do not need rework.

passthroughFindings.subsystem: Silkscreen legibility — reference designator 'U12' vs C62
passthroughFindings.summary: Estimated (not tool-confirmed): U12's reference-designator text, transformed to board coordinates, lands at approximately (223.65, 100) mm, which is close to/likely overlapping the silkscreen footprint of neighboring capacitor C62 (body roughly centered at 222.5, 100).
passthroughFindings.evidence: This is the weakest finding in this report — derived from an estimated text width (1x1mm font, ~2-2.5mm for 'U12') combined with component bounding boxes, not a rendered/measured silkscreen check, because the tool that would normally confirm this (get_footprint_info / rendered board view) was unavailable for the whole session.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Treat as a hint to visually check, not a confirmed defect — re-run get_component_geometry or a rendered 2D/SVG export on U12 and C62 once the KiCad MCP backend recovers.

passthroughFindings.summary: 3 global fiducials (FID1 near x=40.5, FID2 near x=153, FID3 near x=259) are reasonably triangulated across the board's unusual 250x50mm aspect ratio, but no local fiducials exist near any of the three 0.5mm-pitch fine-pitch ICs (U1 LQFP-144, U11/U12 QFN-24) — each relies on a global fiducial roughly 30-45mm away.
passthroughFindings.evidence: Component-list position data (U11 at x=85, nearest fiducial FID1 at x=40.5, ~44.5mm away; U12 at x=227, nearest fiducial FID3 at x=259, ~32mm away; U1 at x=150, FID2 at x=153, ~3mm away and adequately covered). Not a hard violation at 0.5mm pitch (local fiducials are more commonly mandated below 0.4mm pitch or for BGA/CSP), but the board's unusual length makes global-fiducial correction accuracy more sensitive to panel stretch at the far ends where U11/U12 sit.
passthroughFindings.recommendation: Optional: consider a local fiducial pair near U11 and near U12 given their distance from the nearest global fiducial, especially since both are also the parts with the missing-courtyard finding above.

result.synthesis:
# Board3 Pre-Fabrication Review — Synthesis Report

**Board:** `kicad/board3/ProPrj_New Project_2026-07-15_23-14-34_2026-07-27.kicad_pcb` (250.254 × 50.254 mm, 4-layer, ~144 footprints), branch `fix/board3-warning-inbox`
**Inputs:** 6 specialist reviewers + adversarial verification. 6 findings survived independent refutation attempts (CONFIRMED); 0 findings were refuted; 17 MEDIUM/LOW reported as-is.

---

## Reviewer verdict summary — and where they disagree

| Reviewer | Verdict |
|---|---|
| fab-readiness | FAB-READY WITH WARNINGS |
| drc-routing | DRC-CLEAN (0 violations, 0 unconnected, independently re-verified two ways) |
| adversarial-ee | NOT fab-ready (POR/strapping FAILS, overcurrent protection FAILS) |
| simplicity | Clean; one optional BOM simplification (U4) |
| dfm | No JLCPCB capability ceiling breached; unconfirmed design margins |
| dfa | ASSEMBLY RISK |

### Explicit conflicts

1. **Overall verdict conflict — fab-readiness vs adversarial-ee.** fab-readiness says "FAB-READY WITH WARNINGS"; adversarial-ee says "not fab-ready from an electrical-robustness standpoint." These are not reconcilable by scope alone: fab-readiness reviewed sourcing/BOM mechanics and found only warnings, while adversarial-ee found a CONFIRMED datasheet violation (RSTN sequencing) and a CONFIRMED protection gap (no fuse). The adversarial findings survived refutation; the conflict resolves in adversarial-ee's favor. **The board is not fab-ready as it stands.**

2. **"DRC-clean" vs real placement defects — drc-routing/dfm vs dfa.** drc-routing and dfm both report a genuine 0-violation DRC at all severities. dfa demonstrates this is partly *structural blindness*, not cleanliness: (a) the AW9523BTQR footprint has **zero courtyard geometry**, so courtyard checks on U11/U12 pass vacuously; (b) the project sets `min_silk_clearance = 0.0`, so silk-over-pad can never fail; (c) via-in-pad is not a KiCad DRC rule at all (dfm concurs). The DRC result is real and valuable — but three of the confirmed/reported defect classes live exactly in its blind spots. Do not read "0 violations" as covering courtyard, silk-over-pad, or via-in-pad on this board.

3. **Bulk capacitance already trimmed vs still oversized — simplicity vs adversarial-ee.** simplicity credits the project with having already cut "880uF of clustered THT bulk caps to 66uF sited at the loads"; adversarial-ee measures **C2 + C16 = 440uF still on the +3V3 rail today**, ~6.5× above the TPS563201's documented D-CAP2 stability window (20–68uF). Both cite project history, but they describe different remaining states. Adversarial-ee's number is against the current BOM/netlist snapshot and matches the project's own open plan items (U13/U14), so treat 440uF-still-present as the operative fact — the trim simplicity describes either didn't reach C2/C16 or was a different cap group.

---

## Ranked findings

### CRITICAL

**1. AW9523B RSTN hard-tied to /+5V on both U11 and U12 — violates mandatory power-on sequencing** *(adversarial-ee, CONFIRMED)*
Netlist proves both RSTN pins (pin 23) are members of the same net as VCC — zero series impedance, no RC. The AW9523B datasheet (V2.4, POWER ON section, Fig. 6) requires RSTN held low ~100us after VCC before release, "otherwise, the device may work incorrectly." This matters more than usual because the POR-default GPIO-HIGH state is the **only** passive mechanism protecting the eight telltale LEDs after KTD17 removed the series resistors and DMOS driver — and that safety argument depends on the chip's POR logic completing correctly, which is exactly what the unimplemented sequencing step guards. A vehicle 5V rail will produce fast brownout/recovery cycles.
**Fix:** RC delay or supervisor output on RSTN for both ICs; or, if hard-tied is kept, an explicit many-cycle brownout bench soak — asserted datasheet defaults are not sufficient.

### HIGH

**2. No overcurrent protection on either external power input** *(adversarial-ee, CONFIRMED)*
Full BOM contains no fuse/PTC of any kind. DC1 (barrel) feeds Q2/U6 ideal-diode ORing directly — reverse-polarity only, no current limit. A stale schematic note references a "dedicated 5V/15A supply"; if that rating is real, the gap is worse, not better.
**Fix:** Resettable PTC (or fuse) between DC1 and Q2/U6 sized to actual load; resolve or delete the 15A annotation.

**3. U2 QSPI NOR flash (W25Q512JVEIQ, C7389628) at 4 units live JLCPCB stock** *(fab-readiness, CONFIRMED)*
Exact-part stock = 4; sibling variants are at 3/0/0. Extended part, qty 1, required. An order can bounce at fulfillment. Secondary: U1 (STM32H755ZIT6, C730212) at stock = 37 — survivable but re-check at order time.
**Fix:** Re-verify immediately before order; pre-qualify a pin-compatible W25Q512JV alternative.

**4. AW9523BTQR footprint has no courtyard geometry (U11, U12) — DRC blind spot on the two highest-diagnosis-risk ICs** *(dfa, CONFIRMED)*
Zero F.CrtYd/B.CrtYd in either footprint instance or the library file. Courtyard checks pass because there is nothing to test. Manual envelope reconstruction puts U12's body ~0.4–0.55mm from LED6's body — tight and never machine-checked.
**Fix:** Add ~4.3×4.3mm F.CrtYd to the footprint in JLCImport.pretty; re-run courtyard checks; eyeball U12 vs LED6 meanwhile.

**5. No silkscreen polarity mark on 3 of 8 telltale LEDs (LED4, LED6, LED7)** *(dfa, CONFIRMED)*
Their footprints carry only two symmetric silk lines; the polarity triangle exists only on F.Fab, which is not printed. The other five LED footprints all have visible silk marks. Failure mode is exactly the "wrong indicator lit, untraceable to placement" scenario for the field-diagnosis-critical telltales.
**Fix:** Add visible cathode marks on F.SilkS to the two affected footprint library files before fab.

**6. Unwindowed 100% paste apertures on all three exposed-pad parts (U11/U12 QFN-24 EP 2.8×2.8mm; U2 WSON-8 EP 5.2×4.65mm)** *(dfa, CONFIRMED)*
Board-wide grep confirms zero paste-margin/windowing anywhere. Solid EP paste is a well-documented cause of voiding, float, and tombstoning (IPC-7093).
**Fix:** Segment EP paste apertures to ~50–70% coverage before ordering the stencil.

### MEDIUM (reported as-is, not independently verified)

**7. +3V3 bulk capacitance (C2+C16 = 440uF) ~6.5× above TPS563201 D-CAP2 stability window** *(adversarial-ee; see Conflict 3)* — independently justified by the buck's own spec regardless of the backlight-current gate that has been blocking it. Reduce toward 20–68uF.

**8. C67 schematic/BOM value mismatch** *(fab-readiness)* — Value "22uF" but sourced to C19702, a 10uF/10V/0603 part; the PCB footprint's own Value already says "10uF", so schematic and board actively disagree. The JLCPCB BOM ships the wrong label either way. Decide which is electrically intended and make the three artifacts agree.

**9. Board-edge clearance: P1/P2 terminal blocks ~0.195mm and DC1 ~0.224mm courtyard-to-edge** *(dfa)* — inside typical ±0.1–0.2mm routing/depaneling tolerance; a deviation could clip connector flanges. Nudge inward 0.3–0.5mm.

**10. USBC1 courtyard extends ~0.37mm past the left board edge** *(dfa)* — real pads are >3mm clear; nudge or record an explicit edge-launch exception.

**11. U3/L2 courtyard overlap (0.254 × 4.3mm)** *(dfa)* — no pad overlap; likely normal tight buck layout, but the height mismatch warrants a GUI look or a 0.3mm nudge.
